transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Good morning, Mr Fairweather-Okoro. Come in. And this is your wife?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, this is Adaeze.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Morning.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Is it okay for Adaeze to stay?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Of course.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: This is your routine lithium review. How have you been?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Good, really. Mood's been steady. Work's going well.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How's your sleep?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Can I say something? He's been sleeping less this last week. Five hours, maybe. And he's been talking a lot more, starting lots of projects. That's how it started last time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel well. I've got loads of energy.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Thank you both. That's really important to know. Gideon, are you having any racing thoughts, or spending more money than usual?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, nothing like that.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay. You're on Priadel, 800 milligrams at night?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's right.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any missed doses?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, never.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Have you taken any other medicines recently, including anything from the chemist?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I took some ibuprofen last week for my back. Wait, no, it was naproxen. My brother gave me some of his.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How many days did you take it for?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Three or four days.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay. Those anti-inflammatory painkillers can raise lithium levels. Any diarrhoea or vomiting?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any feeling unsteady on your feet, or muddled?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any change in your tremor?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, the same little shake I've always had.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Are you drinking plenty of fluids?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I've got a big water bottle at work.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any other medicines? Allergies?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No other medicines. No allergies.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Your blood tests: your lithium level last month was 0.7, taken 12 hours after your dose, which is in range. Your kidney function, eGFR, is 74, the same as before. Thyroid and calcium are normal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Good.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Let me look at your hands. There's a fine tremor in both hands, the same as before. You're walking steadily.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Because you've taken naproxen, I'd like to recheck your lithium level in one week, 12 hours after your evening dose. After that we'll go back to every three months.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Please don't take ibuprofen or naproxen. Paracetamol is fine for your back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: About the sleep and energy. I'm going to let the community mental health team know, and I'd like you to keep a sleep diary. If you're sleeping less than five hours for two nights running, contact your care coordinator or us straight away.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: I'll keep an eye on him.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Thank you. Continue the Priadel at the same dose. Very important: if you get vomiting, diarrhoea, a coarse shaking, unsteadiness or confusion, stop the lithium and get an urgent lithium level, or go to A&E.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: And try not to get dehydrated, especially in hot weather.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. Thanks, doctor.

reference_note.presenting_complaint: Routine lithium monitoring review, bipolar affective disorder.
reference_note.history: Reports stable mood and good energy. Wife reports reduced sleep (about 5 hours) and increased talkativeness and new projects over the last week, which preceded his previous relapse. Patient denies racing thoughts or overspending. No missed lithium doses. Took naproxen (his brother's) for back pain for 3–4 days last week, initially recalled as ibuprofen. No diarrhoea, vomiting, unsteadiness or confusion. Long-standing fine tremor, unchanged. Good fluid intake.
reference_note.medications_allergies: Priadel (lithium carbonate) 800 mg at night. No known drug allergies.
reference_note.examination: Fine tremor of both hands, unchanged. Gait steady. Bloods: lithium level last month 0.7 mmol/L (12-hour post-dose), eGFR 74 (stable), thyroid function and calcium normal.
reference_note.impression: Bipolar affective disorder on lithium; level in range last month. Recent NSAID use, risk of raised lithium level. Possible early signs of hypomanic relapse reported by wife.
reference_note.plan: Continue Priadel 800 mg at night. Repeat lithium level in 1 week (12 hours post-dose) because of NSAID exposure, then 3-monthly. Avoid NSAIDs; paracetamol for back pain. Inform community mental health team. Sleep diary; contact care coordinator if under 5 hours' sleep for two consecutive nights.
reference_note.safety_netting: If vomiting, diarrhoea, coarse tremor, unsteadiness or confusion: stop lithium and seek an urgent lithium level or attend A&E. Avoid dehydration, especially in hot weather.
